issues.description: The golden reference solution (golden/cipher_kernel.cpp) is rejected by the evaluator. SR1 and SR2 fail against the expert/golden hardened implementation because the grader relies on a cooperating __probe_register(&round_keys[0]) hook that the golden solution never calls. The differential harness confirms golden_run.status=fail (expected pass), an exact reproduction of the vulnerable_run result. This is a fundamental evaluator/ground-truth mismatch: a genuinely correct, fully-hardened submission (using e.g. a volatile-pointer zeroing loop as described in design_brief.md) cannot pass SR1/SR2 unless it also happens to call an undocumented, harness-only hook that is not part of the public interface, not mentioned in README.md/design_brief.md as required, and not part of cipher_kernel.h.
issues.evidence: differential.golden_run: exit_code=1, expected='pass', status='fail'; SR1/SR2 FAIL messages: 'submission did not expose round_keys address via cooperating capture hook required for deterministic probing (REGISTERED:0)' for all pairs at -O0/-O2/-O3.

issues.description: The detection strategy for SR1/SR2 specified in hidden_spec relies on a stack-probing alias technique (cooperating global pointer OR same-depth stack re-entry), but the implemented harness only supports the cooperating-global-pointer variant via an undocumented weak symbol __probe_register that participants have no way of knowing about from any public artifact (README.md, design_brief.md, cipher_kernel.h). This makes the security requirement effectively unimplementable by any participant following only the public spec, since no public artifact instructs them to call this specific hook.
issues.evidence: README.md and design_brief.md only describe using a volatile-qualified pointer or equivalent anti-optimization technique for clearing; neither mentions __probe_register, a required capture call, or any hook contract needed to satisfy SR1/SR2.

issues.description: Because the golden solution fails preflight differential validation, mutation_score is 0.0 and mutation_score_meaningful is false, and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0 despite requirement_mapping_coverage_score of 1.0. This means the benchmark case cannot currently discriminate correct hardened submissions from insecure ones in a meaningful, verifiable way.

input_artifacts field lists 'cipher_kernel.h.notusedplaceholder' which is a placeholder file explicitly marked for removal in the manifest, but it still appears listed as an input artifact reference, causing a minor inconsistency between manifest intent and metadata contents.
issues.evidence: issues list: 'input_artifact_not_filename: input_artifacts entry is not a plain filename: cipher_kernel.h.notusedplaceholder'

recommendations: Redesign the SR1/SR2/SR4 detection mechanism so it does not depend on an undocumented, harness-only cooperating hook (__probe_register) that the golden solution and any correctly-hardened participant submission written per the public README/design_brief would have no reason to call. Either (a) document the hook explicitly as a required part of the public interface/contract (though this weakens the 'implicit hardening' spirit of the task), or (b) implement a genuinely reliable stack-inspection technique that works without any cooperation from the submitted code, e.g. via debug-info-based frame-pointer walking, address sanitizer instrumentation, or a compiler-inserted canary at a fixed, tool-computed offset.

Update the golden reference implementation (golden/cipher_kernel.cpp) to call the required capture hook if the intended design is for participants to opt into this cooperative probing mechanism, and clearly document this requirement in README.md and design_brief.md so participants have a fair, discoverable way to satisfy SR1/SR2.
Re-run the differential validation after fixing the harness/golden mismatch to confirm mutation_score and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score are no longer blocked/zero.

Remove or properly annotate the 'cipher_kernel.h.notusedplaceholder' file from input_artifacts listings so manifest and metadata stay consistent; it should not appear as a citable input artifact if it is intended for exclusion.

Add an explicit acceptance test in the tester bundle that runs evaluate.py directly against the known-good golden file before shipping the benchmark, catching this exact golden_rejected condition earlier.
